A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MARS-SQL, with matching core methodology and original benchmark results. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite extensive additions and reorganization in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original BIRD, Spider, and Spider-DK evaluations, component ablations, interaction-budget experiments, and trajectory-selection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds SParC evaluation, resource profiling, scaling and budget comparisons, and behavioral analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same GRPO-trained Grounding and Generation agents, execution-based rewards, ReAct interaction loop, and SFT-trained probability-based Validation agent. The prompts and selection procedure are retained. Larger-model experiments and proposed deployment optimizations do not establish a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains BIRD, Spider, and Spider-DK and adds SParC evaluation in Appendix D. SParC introduces questions dependent on preceding conversational context, substantively extending coverage beyond the earlier single-question benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Qwen3-coder-30B and removes the separate Qwen2.5-coder SFT/RL rows from v1 Table 2. Appendices F-G add reasoning-model comparisons, high-budget SQL-R1 voting, a three-model ensemble, and 14B/32B shared-model multitask baselines. The original trajectory-selection comparators remain.

E3.justification: New designs include approximately 22-second matched-budget comparisons, 64-sample voting, joint generation/validation budget sweeps, and model-size controls. Arctic-Text2SQL-R1's reported main-table size changes from 7B to 32B without changed scores. v2 also states RL batch size 64 while retaining 128 in Table 4, leaving that training setting unresolved rather than establishing a consistent rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled component isolation, parameter-scaling and efficiency analyses, interaction-length distributions, schema-complexity analysis, and cases examining semantic and pagination errors. These substantially extend v1's component, turn-limit, candidate-count, and selection studies, which remain after relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Newly specified inference sampling counts and average resource measurements do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original BIRD-dev/Spider-test/Spider-DK scores remain 77.84/89.75/78.13%. New results include SParC accuracy of 85.78%, 78.62% for the scaled-generator configuration, and extensive cost and behavioral measurements. New Table 7 reports GPT-5 Spider accuracy as 77.10%, conflicting with 78.39% in both main tables; this is an unresolved reporting discrepancy, not an established performance decline.

T1.justification: The trajectory and MDP definitions, GRPO objectives, reward functions, and probability-based selection rule retain their mathematical substance. Some equations become inline text or prose, but no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The central interactive three-agent contribution and headline accuracy claims remain. v2 qualifies novelty as making the workflow trainable and adds the claim that gains are not explained by parameter count or inference time alone. These refine and extend the retained core contribution.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes indispensable components and strong synergy across benchmarks. v2 instead explains their unequal, complementary effects, particularly grounding's dependence on schema complexity and verification's larger contribution. It also adds substantial interpretations of interaction efficiency, parameter scaling, and deployment trade-offs, explicitly acknowledging the three-agent cost.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 600/160 RL training steps, approximately 13 hours on four H800 GPUs, eight verification rounds, A6000/32-CPU profiling, and sequential deployment and memory details. Prompts and the code URL persist. The separate commitment to releasing code and models is omitted; actual resource availability cannot be inferred from that omission.

R1.justification: The four related-work themes remain largely intact. v2 adds a specific contrast with MSc-SQL, cites MTSQL-R1 and additional agent, benchmark, and model literature, and drops references including MetaGPT and SQLGlot. Positioning shifts toward trainable interaction, but the broader research context remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contributions, component interpretation, conclusion, and ethics/impact discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Experimental headings and appendices are reorganized, including separating generation prompts from behavioral analysis. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, removes v1's capability-comparison table, adds agent-count columns and numerous analytical tables, and introduces an accuracy-latency plot. Existing figures are relocated or redrawn; Figure 3 changes axis limits and expands its caption, while Figure 4 changes colors.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in evaluating v1's results: it explicitly accounts for the three 7B agents, adds parameter- and time-budget controls, documents deployment costs, and replaces blanket component-synergy assertions with more qualified explanations. These substantially improve transparency and assessment of the contribution. Conflicting batch sizes and baseline scores, plus unsupported SFT-efficiency extrapolations, weaken some additions but do not outweigh the gains from the new controls and clearer practical limitations.
